roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Ratepayer Protection Act (H R 9340)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill tells state utility regulators to consider making very large power users, such as data centers using 100 megawatts or more, pay the full extra cost of grid upgrades built to serve them. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

post.text:
Yesterday, the Ratepayer Protection Act passed the House with overwhelming bipartisan support, 417-3. I was proud to support this legislation because hardworking Americans should not be forced to pay higher electric bills to power massive data centers.

Data centers should pay

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
roll_calls.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

roll_calls.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

post.text:
As an original cosponsor of the Stop Insider Trading Act, I’m extremely pleased that it passed the House.

Transparency and accountability are essential for public confidence in our government. From my first day in Congress, I made a commitment not to trade individual stocks
